I can confidently say that I loved this game !

I’ve played a lot of detective and mystery games over the years, and it’s not easy to create one that feels both engaging and memorable. Triangle Tower managed to do exactly that. The characters were charming, the story kept me invested, and the overall atmosphere was incredibly pleasant from start to finish. The puzzles struck a great balance between challenge and enjoyment. They made me think without becoming frustrating, which is something many detective games struggle with. The music, character development, world-building, and puzzle design all felt carefully crafted and thoughtfully executed.

The game gave me strong Professor Layton vibes, but in a more modern and advanced way. It reminded me of why I fell in love with mystery games in the first place.

If I had one small criticism, it would be the final solution to the mystery. For me, it wasn’t the most convincing or intuitive conclusion. That said, I understand that the story leans a little more into fantasy elements at that point, so it didn’t ruin the experience. Overall, congratulations to the developers. This was a wonderful experience, and I sincerely hope we get more games featuring the same detectives and characters in the future. I would happily play another adventure with them.

The very first thing to say is: this game is amazing, from the mystery to the art style, from the music to the character designs, from the UI to the stupid little quips. One of the best point-and-click games i can think of, and I am absolutely STOKED for the sequel The Mermaid Mask to come out. This game is almost perfect; almost. Like every good murder mystery movie, there is a compelling hook-- the murder of a young artist in a bizarre mansion full of eccentric characters, seemingly stabbed by her own final artwork. And, like every good murder mystery, there is a deeper spider's web of mystery and conspiracy that underlies the surface. As you gather more evidence, solve more puzzles, and question the (wonderfully drawn, written, and voice-acted) suspects, you get so drawn into this deeper mystery that you almost forget about the murder all together. Unfortunately, it feels like the game does the same. While the grand conspiracy is incredibly narratively satisfying, and sets up the series' future installments very well, the actual conclusion to the murder is not very satisfying. There is a beautiful network of rivalries and relationships and secrets going on between all the characters, and yet the murderer's motivation ends up feeling very forced? As if the author(s) didn't have an real idea for WHY this character would commit the murder, just that it was going to be them. And this is such a shame because the rest of the mystery-- including elements that tie into and play out along side the final reveal-- are so incredibly done! The atmosphere during the murderer's confession is genuinely so ominous and terrifying: there is a moment, right before the confession, of where you examine the bloody painting and gather your final piece of tangible evidence: and you see something that had been in front of your face the entire time. And it sent genuine chills down my spine, even on this recent replay. And then you learn everything the murder is driven by, and what they've been up to, and everything regarding the second mystery-- and its incredible. But then they share their reason for the murder and it falls so flat.  And then a final twist, and it sends another jolt of chills! And in the final ending scene of the game, characters tied to the murder victim get to have a quiet, emotional moment that jerks your heart and reminds you that these characters are so well written and well loved by whoever made them.

If you love point-and-click, puzzle, and/or mystery games, I very highly recommend playing this game and following these creators into the sequel! Its genuinely impressive that there is only one gripe I have with this game-- and while the discovery of the mysteries elements are done perfectly, it is disappointing that the motivation at the core of the murder feels like a hand-wave or an after thought.

[Edit] Also the Music Player and concept art menus are a phenomenal touch; this game has absolutely gorgeous music that i could absolutely imagine buying as a soundtrack, and the character designs are absolutely stunning (I think Penny Pointer has one of my favorite designs in anything, ever? and Hawkshaw is the kind of character i would eat up as a webcomic protagonist. Just, absolutely stunning game.)
Overall a really beautiful and thrilling game followed abruptly by an extremely clunky and confusing ending 7/10

Tangle Tower is an absolute delight of a detective game, with multiple intertwined mysteries that were all extremely interesting. Every single interaction and examination in the game is fully voice acted, and all the voice actors performed masterfully (though I do have my favorite).

I only found two possible issues with the game; there are a lot of (fully voice acted) interactions, and once you narrow down your cross-examinations to the last 2-3 people, it can feel like you're randomly presenting evidence to people just to see if you can get a contradiction out of them. For this, I highly recommend using the Hint button to point to which room you are supposed to be looking in.

Finally, not all aspects of all mysteries were completely wrapped up and explained. This isn't necessarily a bad thing, but there were some things left up to interpretation by the player. The main mystery was completely explained, but some motives and other background details about the setting don't feel fully justified.

All in all, Tangle Tower shows the amount of love and care put into the game at every step. From the charming voice acting, to the beautiful art and animation, all the way to the absolutely hilarious dialogue, Tangle Tower captivated me from start to end.

[b]Tangle Tower[/b] is a wonderfully charming game about two budding detectives trying to solve a murder case that is just as twisted as its title name. 95% of this game is a fun, colorful, and creative mystery puzzle game. The characters are so lovingly realized, with unique musical motifs and bouncy squash-and-stretch art giving each of them a wholly distinct identity. The writing is punchy and funny to boot. But the game stumbles at the finish line - rather than letting you point the finger at the culprit, it just hands the answer to you on a silver platter, the villain explaining their motivations in no uncertain terms. For a Whoddunnit mystery, this just feels bad, and it is especially strange because the first Detective Grimoire game got this part right. But even with that in mind, the game is no less charming or fun - I would still wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who is a fan of mystery puzzle games in the vein of Professor Layton.

I downloaded this game after completing its predecessor, Detective Grimoire: Secret of the Swamp (SotS). I am a big fan of thrillers and mysteries in all forms (books, movies, games, etc.) and after replaying some of the Nancy Drew games from my youth, I was hoping to find a new series to explore. 

The developers definitely listened to the feedback they received from SotS and made improvements all around. Navigation between areas is smoother, the interface is more intuitive, the plot is more intricate, and the characters have more specialized interactions during investigation with a greater overall depth to them. It took me around 3.5 hours to complete SotS 100% with all achievements, but Tangle Tower took me closer to a full 6 hours to do the same. 

Though the case seems fairly straightforward at the beginning of the game, I found myself becoming increasingly engaged as I began to speak with more characters, uncover new clues, and unlock new areas. I felt very immersed and completely lost track of time (regrettably, I stayed up until 1 am to finish despite needing to wake up for work at 6 am because I just couldn't bring myself to exit the game). While it is not necessary to play SotS first, there are some callbacks and Easter Eggs in Tangle Tower that are more fun if you've played it. I highly recommend this game, but be aware that it can get very intense and disturbing at times, especially near the end. While there aren't jump scares, sexual violence, or gore, I would say that between the puzzle difficulty and plotline material/complexity, this game is most appropriate for ages 13+.

This is the second point-and-click adventure of Detective Grimoire available on Steam, but it is pretty much stand-alone and not a sequel. It's probably why it's not mentioned anywhere on the store page. The advantages of playing Dectective Grimoire first are that it's cheaper, easier and shorter. However, Tangle Tower is improved in almost every aspect, including graphics. Very good characters with personality. Excellent voice acting all around especially for Grimoire's assistant, Sally. The soundtrack was unobstrusive and lovely, with music suitable for each suspect. I loved the art style. It was different and distinctive. I also liked the little character animations when characters talked (or not in the case of Flora) very much although they tended to repeat. Lots of described hotspots and clues, which is something I particularly appreciate in a mystery game. No hotspot indicator, but it wasn't necessary.

No inventory and therefore no traditional inventory-based puzzles, but case files and self-contained logic puzzles. Pretty clever puzzles and I don't recall seeing them used before. They might not have been lying about the "unique puzzles" on the store page. They could be challenging, but I was never stuck that long because of gradual hints given when you failed. The best part for me, constructing deductions out of images and sentence fragments, was back but there seemed to be fewer of them. Or perhaps they were more spaced out. I enjoyed solving each suspect's personal mystery. I think they were optional, but I'm not sure. The overall murder mystery was quite smartly done except for a few plot holes, and that long confession followed by an abrupt ending. Tangle Tower  was a very good game and I'm looking forward to the upcoming case: The Mermaid Mask.

我个人玩过挺多市面上的推理、解谜以及逃脱类游戏，这款游戏给我的整体印象很不错。首先它的画风非常好，其次配音也很优秀，无论是角色配音，还是每一个细节道具点击的声音，都做得很出色。这两点其实还可以进一步细化打磨。

不过游戏的中文翻译还有提升空间，不是那么精致，但整体玩下来还是挺顺畅的。另外，有不少内容需要理解英文原意，才能感受到其中的乐趣，玩起来也会更顺畅。

解谜趣味性方面，没有什么特别难的内容，都是非常基础的解谜设计——我指的是游戏里那些需要解谜才能拿到线索、获取证据的盒子、机关，难度都比较低，没有太大挑战。

推理方面则很合乎常理，不需要过多额外思考，只要认真看、认真听，多和角色对话、多互动沟通，基本上就能明白他们在聊什么，而且证据的指向性也比较明显。

最值得推荐的一点，是故事剧情线做得非常好。不仅有反转，故事结构也很完整，每个人物形象都很清晰。需要说明的是，它并不是一款强解谜、强推理的游戏——如果是奔着纯粹的解谜推理去玩，不是很建议；但如果喜欢综合性较强的游戏，尤其是偏爱剧情向、喜欢沉浸式体验故事的，这款游戏会很合适。它的故事很出色，而且每个角色都有值得喜爱的地方，也都有自己的底线。

这款游戏对于喜欢收集成就的玩家来说也很合适。游戏里的成就一共只有10个，玩下来基本上都能解锁，没有什么需要重复操作的地方，只要在游戏过程中多点一点、仔细找到所有线索，就能顺利拿到全部成就。

一言难尽，这剧情用高开低走，虎头蛇尾都不够了，简直是一泻千里，前面每个人物对各种证据的看法都很有个性很有趣，主线也挺有悬念的，妥妥的一个好游戏模板，但打到最后半小时突然就拉稀了，给人的感觉像是剧本早就写好了，一大堆庞大的世界观设定，但是做到后面发现没经费了，然后就只能让凶手把世界观设定设定，杀人动机，杀人手法自己一股脑全说出来了。这游戏给人的感觉像是剥洋葱剥到最后发现最里面已经烂了，好像剥掉最里面的里面烂掉的部分，外面的部分还能吃，但是你还是能闻到那股腐烂的味道从而只能整个洋葱全扔了。

如果你是冲着画风，配音，美术，音乐和人物有趣的小对话来的，我还是推荐的。但如果你的预期是一个正经的推理游戏，我的建议是绕道

초중반까지 몰입도가 높고, 흥미로운 게임 경험을 선사합니다. 아름다운 아트워크와 흥미롭고 수많은 이야기를 담고 있는 탑의 비주얼 디자인을 하나하나 탐색해나가며 저택에 얽힌 역사와 그 안에서 사는 사람들의 이야기를 생생하게 들을 수 있습니다. 캐릭터와의 대화가 재미있게 구성되어 있습니다. 빌드업이 탄탄하여 어떤 이야기가 숨겨져 있을지, 어떤 음모가 도사리고 있는지 끊임없이 호기심을 자극합니다. 허투루 만들어진 낭비되는 캐릭터가 없는 것처럼 보이고, 아트워크 하나하나가 다 힌트를 담고 있습니다. 피해자도 단순한 가련한 피해자 A가 아니라 하나의 캐릭터로서 생동감 있게 존재감을 발휘합니다. 

그러나 스토리는 중반부터 힘을 잃기 시작합니다. 쌓아올렸던 빌드업을 토대로 달성해야 할 목표는 갑자기 힘을 잃어버리고, 수많은 떡밥이나 의문점은 해결되지 않은 채 흐지부지 넘어갑니다. 엔딩은 갑작스럽고, 많은 이야기가 준비되어 있었으나 미처 펼쳐 보일 기회를 얻지 못한 채 게임은 종지부를 찍습니다. 

좋은 미스터리 추리물은 엔딩이 좋아야 합니다. 그러나 아쉽게도 이 게임은 그 '괜찮은 결말'을 그려내는 데에는 실패했습니다. 그럼에도 구성은 몹시도 흥미롭고, 짧은 플레이타임 덕에 수많은 노력이 헛되이 무너지는 실망감의 무게감은 다행히 적습니다.  여러 부분을 유저의 상상에 맡긴 채 끝나버리지만 이 안에 어떤 이야기나 행복과 불행이 교차하고 있었을지 짐작할 수 있는 힌트는 널려 있습니다. 

이 시리즈에 차기작이 26년에 나온다던데, 스토리 부분에서 좀 더 보완을 많이 해서 양질의 시나리오를 갖춰 들고 오면 좋겠습니다. 추리물은 역시 내러티브와 결말이 중요하다고 봅니다.
